newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran reiterates it won't seek to kill Rushdie.
newsitem.headline: Iran reiterates it won't seek to kill Rushdie.

text.p: Iran has reiterated that a death edict against British author Salman Rushdie was irrevocable, but added it would not send anyone to kill him.

The foreign ministry said in a statement published in the daily Jomhuri Eslami on Tuesday that Iran's stand remained unchanged and was based on "the irrevocability of the fatwa by the Imam (late Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini) and...Iran not sending any commandos (to kill Rushdie)."

The statement, made in reply to the hardline conservative newspaper which had warned against new negotiations with the European Union over Rushdie, appeared to be the first time that Iran issues this stand in writing. Senior officials had repeatedly expressed the same position verbally.

British media reports said in June several EU states backed a deal under which letters would be exchanged, with the EU saying the fatwa was "valid and irrevocable" in return for a written guarantee from Tehran that it would not send agents to kill Rushdie.
Iran's government had earlier rejected an EU request for a written declaration that it would not carry out the fatwa and would seek to restrain Iranians from trying to do so.
The fatwa, or religious edict, was issued by Khomeini in 1989, condemning Rushdie to death for alleged blasphemy against Islam in his novel "The Satanic Verses".
Iranian officials say the fatwa is a religious matter unrelated to state policies and no one can cancel it.
